 Texas lawmaker proposes raising minimum wage to $15 an hour
 AUSTIN, Texas — Texas workers earning minimum wage could see their hourly pay more than double under a proposed bill that would raise the state's minimum wage from $7.25 to $15 an hour.
 House Bill 132, introduced by state Rep. Armando Walle, would require employers to pay workers at least $15 an hour or the federal minimum wage, whichever is higher.
 The proposal would increase the current minimum wage by $7.75 an hour, giving someone working 40 hours a week an additional $310 before taxes. That translates to roughly $16,120 more annually for a full-time employee.
 Texas currently follows the federal minimum wage of $7.25 an hour, which has remained unchanged since July 2009, when it increased from $6.55.
 Under the proposed legislation, the new $15 hourly minimum would take effect Sept. 1, 2027, if approved by state lawmakers and signed into law.
 The bill would also repeal a section of the Texas Labor Code dealing with the state's minimum wage requirements.
 For now, the proposal is just that — a proposal. It must make its way through the Texas Legislature before any changes could take effect.
